Title: pkgconf: dependency names in .pc files are treated as filesystem paths, allowing memory exhaustion and loading of .pc files outside the search path
URL: https://github.com/pkgconf/pkgconf/security/advisories/GHSA-qcp5-98c5-hvh7
Acquired: 2026-11-14
Snippets:
libpkgconf resolves the module names listed in a pc(5) file's `Requires`, `Requires.private`, `Requires.shared` and `Conflicts` fields with the same lookup used for command-line queries. That lookup accepts filesystem paths. A crafted pc(5) file can therefore name a dependency by path, which (1) defeats the package cache and cycle detection, causing unbounded memory consumption, and (2) loads pc(5) files from outside the configured search path. ### Details pkgconf_pkg_verify_dependency() passes the dependency name from a pc(5) file directly to pkgconf_pkg_find(). pkgconf_pkg_find() treats the name as a path in two ways: - if the name ends in ".pc" it is opened as a file, and on success the file's directory is appended to the client's search path; - otherwise the name is joined to each search directory as "[dir]/[name].pc", so a name containing "/" or ".." is resolved relative to that directory. A package's id is derived from the basename of the file that was loaded, and the package cache is keyed by that id. A dependency written as "/a" or "./a" loads a.pc and yields a package whose id is "a", but the cache is consulted with the name "/a", which never matches. Every lookup of such a name therefore creates a new package object. The circular-dependency check and the per-traversal visited marker both operate on package objects, so they do not recognize the new object as one already seen. The fix restricts path-based lookup to names given by the user on the command line (dependency nodes flagged PKGCONF_PKG_DEPF_QUERY). Names supplied by a pc(5) file are treated as module names only: a name containing a path separator is not looked up, and a ".pc" suffix is not interpreted as a filename. ### Proof of concept Any pc(5) file which references its own path can reproduce the vulnerability: ``` $ mkdir poc && cd poc $ printf 'Name: a\nVersion: 1\nDescription: a\nRequires: ./a\n' > a.pc $ PKG_CONFIG_PATH=. pkgconf --exists a ```
[...]
Search path escape: a .pc file inside the configured search path can cause .pc files elsewhere on the filesystem to be loaded and can extend the search path. This breaks the isolation that PKG_CONFIG_LIBDIR is relied on to provide, for example keeping host packages out of a cross-compilation sysroot.

#!/usr/bin/env bash

function _guess_prefix() {
  local _GUESS_FILE
  if [ -n "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}" ]; then
    _GUESS_FILE="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)/$(basename "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")"
  elif [ -n "${(%):-%x}" ]; then
    # in zsh use prompt-style expansion to introspect the same information
    # see http://stackoverflow.com/questions/9901210/bash-source0-equivalent-in-zsh
    _GUESS_FILE="$(cd "$(dirname "${(%):-%x}")" && pwd)/$(basename "${(%):-%x}")"
  else
    # This case will be hit outside of conda-build or a properly activated
    # conda environment when not using bash nor zsh. This is a corner case
    _GUESS_FILE="${PWD}/bin/unknown"
  fi
  echo $(dirname $(dirname ${_GUESS_FILE}))
}

function _run_pkgconf() {
  local PC_PREFIX=$(_guess_prefix)
  local PC_PATH_BUILD="$(${PC_PREFIX}/bin/pkgconf.bin --variable pc_path pkg-config)"
  local PC_PATH_HOST=${PC_PATH_BUILD//$PC_PREFIX/${PREFIX:-${CONDA_PREFIX:-$PC_PREFIX}}}

  # conda customization for CDT packages; are we targeting Linux with a cross compiler
  if [[ ${HOST} =~ .*linux.* ]] && [[ $(basename ${CC}) =~ .*-.*-.* ]]; then
    # From https://cgit.freedesktop.org/pkg-config/tree/main.c#n520
    # it can be seen that the logic is:
    # PKG_CONFIG_PATH, if set, always comes first
    # if PKG_CONFIG_LIBDIR is set it comes next
    # .. otherwise PC_PATH_HOST comes next.
    # If we tried to send sysroot paths in via PKG_CONFIG_PATH they would
    # get precedence over PREFIX (pkg_config_pc_path). We never want that.
    # Instead pass PKG_CONFIG_LIBDIR as PC_PATH:SYSROOT and allow the user
    # to take precedence over all that iff PKG_CONFIG_PATH is set.
    SRLIBDIR="$(${CC} -print-sysroot)/usr/lib/pkgconfig"
    if [[ ${CONDA_BUILD_PKG_CONFIG_LOG} == yes ]]; then
      echo "Calling: PKG_CONFIG_LIBDIR=${PKG_CONFIG_LIBDIR}:${PC_PATH_HOST}:$(${CC} -print-sysroot)/usr/share/pkgconfig:${SRLIBDIR} \
        ${PC_PREFIX}/bin/pkgconf.bin --define-prefix --debug "$@" > /tmp/pkgconf-$$.log"
      PKG_CONFIG_LIBDIR="${PKG_CONFIG_LIBDIR}:${PC_PATH_HOST}":"$(${CC} -print-sysroot)/usr/share/pkgconfig:${SRLIBDIR}" \
        ${PC_PREFIX}/bin/pkgconf.bin --define-prefix --debug "$@" >> /tmp/pkgconf-$$.log 2>&1 || true
    fi
    PKG_CONFIG_LIBDIR="${PKG_CONFIG_LIBDIR}:${PC_PATH_HOST}":"$(${CC} -print-sysroot)/usr/share/pkgconfig:${SRLIBDIR}" \
      ${PC_PREFIX}/bin/pkgconf.bin --define-prefix "$@"
  else
    # We might need --define-prefix here sometimes, but would be better off ensuring /usr is replaced by ${prefix}
    # in all source .pc files in our packages. TODO :: Make conda-build / conda-verify detect this.
    # try to determine additionnals /lib arch dir. On 64bits systems, it should be /lib and /lib64, on 32bits it should be /lib and /lib32
    SRLIBDIR=":/usr/lib/pkgconfig:/usr/share/pkgconfig"
    if [[ ${HOSTTYPE} == "" ]]; then
       SRLIBDIRARCH=":/usr/lib$(uname -m | sed 's/x86_//;s/i[3-6]86/32/')/pkgconfig"
    else
       SRLIBDIRARCH=":/usr/lib$(echo ${HOSTTYPE} | sed 's/x86_//;s/i[3-6]86/32/')/pkgconfig"
    fi

    PC_PATH_SYSROOT=${PC_PATH_BUILD//$PC_PREFIX//usr$CONDA_BUILD_SYSROOT}${SRLIBDIRARCH}${SRLIBDIR}
    if [[ ${CONDA_BUILD_PKG_CONFIG_LOG} == yes ]]; then
      echo "Calling: PKG_CONFIG_LIBDIR=${PKG_CONFIG_LIBDIR}:${PC_PATH_HOST}:${PC_PATH_SYSROOT} \
        ${PC_PREFIX}/bin/pkgconf.bin --define-prefix --debug $@ > /tmp/pkgconf-$$.log"
      PKG_CONFIG_LIBDIR="${PKG_CONFIG_LIBDIR}:${PC_PATH_HOST}:${PC_PATH_SYSROOT}" \
        ${PC_PREFIX}/bin/pkgconf.bin --define-prefix --debug "$@" >> /tmp/pkgconf-$$.log 2>&1 || true
    fi
    PKG_CONFIG_LIBDIR="${PKG_CONFIG_LIBDIR}:${PC_PATH_HOST}:${PC_PATH_SYSROOT}" \
      ${PC_PREFIX}/bin/pkgconf.bin --define-prefix "$@"
  fi
}

_run_pkgconf "$@"

Title: pkgconf: dependency names in .pc files are treated as filesystem paths, allowing memory exhaustion and loading of .pc files outside the search path

libpkgconf resolves the module names listed in a pc(5) file's `Requires`, `Requires.private`, `Requires.shared` and `Conflicts` fields with the same lookup used for command-line queries. That lookup accepts filesystem paths. A crafted pc(5) file can therefore name a dependency by path, which (1) defeats the package cache and cycle detection, causing unbounded memory consumption, and (2) loads pc(5) files from outside the configured search path. ### Details pkgconf_pkg_verify_dependency() passes the dependency name from a pc(5) file directly to pkgconf_pkg_find(). pkgconf_pkg_find() treats the name as a path in two ways:
[...]
The fix restricts path-based lookup to names given by the user on the command line (dependency nodes flagged PKGCONF_PKG_DEPF_QUERY). Names supplied by a pc(5) file are treated as module names only: a name containing a path separator is not looked up, and a ".pc" suffix is not interpreted as a filename.
[...]
Search path escape: a .pc file inside the configured search path can cause .pc files elsewhere on the filesystem to be loaded and can extend the search path. This breaks the isolation that PKG_CONFIG_LIBDIR is relied on to provide, for example keeping host packages out of a cross-compilation sysroot.

Title: Conda generates non-relocatable launchers when built with rattler-build
URL: https://github.com/conda/conda/issues/16327
Published: 2026-07-01
Acquired: 2026-09-27
Snippets:
When the `conda` package is built with rattler-build, the generated `bin/conda` and `condabin/conda` launchers use this shebang: ``` #!/usr/bin/env python ``` Because the build prefix is no longer present in these files, rattler-build cannot record them for prefix relocation. After installation, the launchers therefore use whichever Python is first on `PATH`, rather than the Python belonging to the environment where conda is installed. This breaks conda after activating a child environment that has Python but does not have conda. The launcher selects the child environment's Python and fails with: ``` ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'conda' ``` This was reported in [conda-forge/conda-feedstock#304](https://github.com/conda-forge/conda-feedstock/issues/304) and [conda-forge/conda-feedstock#305](https://github.com/conda-forge/conda-feedstock/issues/305) after [conda-forge/conda-feedstock#300](https://github.com/conda-forge/conda-feedstock/pull/300) migrated the feedstock to rattler-build. [conda-forge/conda-feedstock#306](https://github.com/conda-forge/conda-feedstock/pull/306) adds a workaround in the feedstock, but the behavior we need to fix is in conda's launcher generation. ### Minimal reproducer This reproduces on Linux using the affected conda-forge build: ``` rm -rf /tmp/conda-rattler-repro /tmp/conda-rattler-child conda create --yes \ --prefix /tmp/conda-rattler-repro \ --override-channels \ --channel conda-forge \ "conda=26.5.3=py314h9e666f3_1" eval "$(/tmp/conda-rattler-repro/bin/python -m conda shell.bash hook)" conda activate /tmp/conda-rattler-repro conda create --yes \ --prefix /tmp/conda-rattler-child \ --override-channels \ --channel conda-forge \ python conda activate /tmp/conda-rattler-child conda --version ``` The final command should print the conda version. Instead, it raises `ModuleNotFoundError`. ### Root cause `conda init --install` calls `generate_shebang_for_entry_point()` with `with_usr_bin_env=True`. Conda normally converts a long Python path to `/usr/bin/env python`, but it preserves conda-build's intentionally long, relocatable shebang with this special case: ``` if os.environ.get("CONDA_BUILD") == "1" and "/_h_env_placehold" in executable: return shebang ``` Rattler-build also sets `CONDA_BUILD=1`, but its host prefix is named `/host_env_placehold...` rather than `/_h_env_placehold...`. The condition does not match, so conda replaces the absolute shebang before rattler-build can detect and record the prefix.

# Diagnosis

Your switch to `pkgconf` was correct, and the recipe change itself is fine — the failure is a **latent breakage in conda-forge's `libgit2.pc` that was masked by GNU pkg-config**. I reproduced it locally in Docker (same `linux-anvil-x86_64:alma10` + rattler-build setup as CI) and confirmed the root cause empirically.

## What actually happens

1. conda-forge's `libgit2` feedstock deliberately patches its `.pc` file to use `Requires.internal: openssl libpcre2-8 libssh2 zlib` — a **pkgconf-only extension** (the patch even contains the warning *"pkg-config does not support Requires.internal"*).
2. `pkgconf` traverses that whole dependency chain: `libssh2.pc` carries `Requires.private: libcrypto,zlib`, and **`zlib.pc` does not exist in your host environment**, so `pkgconf` exits 1 with `Package 'zlib', required by 'libssh2', not found`. `libgit2-sys`'s build.rs reports *any* probe failure as the generic "system libgit2 not found" message — which is why the log looks like a missing `.pc` file, misleading you toward the `PKG_CONFIG_PATH` red herring.
3. The old `pkg-config` package was GNU pkg-config 0.29.2, which **silently ignores the unknown `Requires.internal` keyword** — the broken chain was never walked, so the probe passed.

Why `libzlib` but no `zlib.pc`: conda-forge's `libgit2` only run-depends on the runtime split `libzlib`, which ships no `.pc` files. The `zlib` dev package *does* ship `zlib.pc` — it just wasn't installed in the host env.

Two corrections to your observations:
- It wasn't linux-specific — **all unix targets failed** (osx_64, osx_arm64, aarch64, ppc64le too; see the check runs on the PR head). win passed only because `LIBGIT2_NO_VENDOR` is unset there, so cargo vendors libgit2.
- The failing probe never had a search-path problem — `libgit2.pc` was found fine.

## Fix

Add `zlib` to the host requirements so the `.pc` chain resolves (verified: full linux_64 build then succeeds, tests pass):

```yaml
  host:
    - if: unix
      then: libgit2
    - if: unix
      then: zlib
```

I committed this on branch `agent-fix-pkgconf-libgit2-probe` (commit `a9fd04d`, with the full rationale in the message).
